summary.text: 话 means “words” or “speech,” and also talk, language, or dialect. It is the simplified form of 話: 言 marks the words-and-speech category, while the traditional graph’s right component is 𠯑, identified as a sound element rather than 舌 “tongue.”

formation.text: Traditional 話 is a phonosemantic compound: 言 contributes the words-and-speech meaning, and 𠯑 is identified as the phonetic component. The reported historical forms differ, so their precise sound correspondence is uncertain. In 话, 言 appears as the reduced side form 讠.

components.text: In 话, 讠 is the reduced side form of 言. In traditional 話, 言 marks the words-and-speech category, a role retained in the simplified character.
In traditional 話, 𠯑 is identified as the phonetic component, not 舌. Its original referent is unclear, and the reported forms do not confirm the precise historical sound correspondence.

sound_limitation.text: The local dataset reports Old Chinese *[k]ʷˤat for 𠯑 and *[g]ʷˤrat-s for 話. The forms differ, and the exact rows are not externally verified; this comparison does not independently confirm the phonetic analysis.

sound.text: The local dataset reports Mandarin guā / huà, Middle Chinese kwat / hwaejH, and Old Chinese *[k]ʷˤat / *[g]ʷˤrat-s for 𠯑 and 話 respectively. The forms differ and do not independently establish the precise correspondence.

history.text: A transmitted seal-script form of 話 is analyzed as 言 plus 𠯑. It does not establish when the graph was created or first used.
话 is the simplified form corresponding to 話, with 言 reduced to 讠. The cited account does not report a change to the right component during simplification.

uncertainties.text: Although 𠯑 is identified as phonetic, its original referent and the precise historical sound relationship remain uncertain. The reported reconstructions use different systems and do not independently confirm that relationship.
The earliest securely dated inscriptional form of 話 has not been established.

senses.text: In 慎爾出話, from 《詩·大雅·抑》, 話 is glossed as 善言, “good words.” This gives an early textual context for the words-or-speech sense, but does not date the graph’s earliest use.

senses.period: Current usage; chronology of these senses unresolved
senses.text: Current meanings include speech, talk, language, and dialect. The available examples do not establish when these uses arose or a dated path from “good words.”

senses.period: Later examples are reported; precise chronology and semantic links unresolved
senses.text: Later examples show uses for narrated stories and informing or telling, but do not establish how or when these uses developed from the words-or-speech sense.

limitations.text: The poem provides an early textual context for “good words,” but its composition and surviving witness dates are unresolved. Later uses are documented, but their chronology and semantic connections are not established.
The glosses and examples do not establish a single sequence of semantic developments; no account of graph borrowing is proposed.

overview.text: 话 means “words” or “speech,” and also talk or language. It is simplified from 話, where 言 marks the speech-related category and 𠯑 is identified as a sound element. The right side is not 舌 “tongue.”

components.text: 讠 is the reduced side form of 言, the speech-related element in this character.
Traditional 話 has 𠯑 on the right as a sound element. The reported forms guā / *[k]ʷˤat and huà / *[g]ʷˤrat-s differ, so the match remains uncertain.

relationships.text: In 话, 讠 is the reduced side form of 言, which marks the words-and-speech category in traditional 話.
Traditional 話 identifies 𠯑 as its phonetic element, though the available comparison does not independently establish the precise historical sound correspondence.
